analysis:
Examined all supplied units, including file metadata, the standalone load patch and surrounding base source. ProviderLoop.swift:685–688 adds a nullable persistence destination for verified managed-load hashes used by next-start registration. The declaration alone establishes no unsafe write or trust escalation; its initialization, writers and registration readers remain outside this batch. Existing process-key generation, signer fallback, slot artifact/cache identities and memory gates show no changed control in these excerpts.
StandaloneServer.swift:1964–1969 removes independent GLM pre-load hash enforcement while retaining weights.recheck(); head:1999–2006 replaces the post-load disk hash with glmLoad.verifiedArtifactSHA256, calls requireGLM5NextLoadedArtifact, and assigns that identity to both bracketing values. Non-GLM loads retain the prior hashing path. This moves the integrity boundary into the managed loader and affects A-004, T-012/T-027 and T-041 artifact/cache bindings. No concrete bypass is demonstrated: the managed loader and validator implementations are not supplied, so their absence here is not evidence of a missing control.
Integration must verify that the managed digest is produced only after verifying the exact bytes used by the loaded container, that nil/mismatch fails closed, and that manifest coverage preserves the former hash contract. Also trace VerifiedWeightHashStore persistence into startup registration for stale or operator-modified records. These are material unresolved contracts, not supported findings. No visible change touches bearer authentication, wire encryption, serving authorization, billing or privileged-helper authority; this limited source pass does not audit their implementations.
